text.en: In football, we kick the ball to teammates and receive it with our feet. Kicking directs the ball to a target; receiving controls it so we do not lose it.

To kick: stand about 5 metres behind the ball and keep your eyes on it. Run towards it.
Keep the non-kicking foot beside the ball. Kick with the inner part or top of the kicking foot.
Swing the arms sideways and follow through in the direction of the kick, smoothly and without a jerk.
To receive: anticipate the direction and speed of the ball and take your position, raising the leg you want to receive with.
Receive the ball with the inside of the foot and move the leg slightly backwards, keeping the other leg firmly on the ground.
Balance your body as the ball touches the ground and try to dribble the ball after receiving.

problem.en: Which part of the foot do you use to receive the ball?

text.en: The book says the inside of the foot.
Move the leg slightly backwards on impact.
Keep the other leg firm for balance.

prompt.en: How do you kick a ball well?

points.en: Kick with the inner part or top of the foot.
Keep the other foot beside the ball.
Receive with the inside of the foot and give a little.
